comparator.name: Psychobiology
comparator.sourceNotes: The dated 2026–2027 study guide verifies the compulsory sixty-credit first and second years. The final year permits a scientific internship/project of 18, 24 or 30 EC and genuinely open elective space. This example retains the permitted 30-EC project and thirty open credits. The project entry threshold and named prerequisite courses are verified; all earlier required courses are completed. No formal route, particular elective package or placement host is invented. The guide’s year-three aggregate is not used as the degree total; its course entry and choice rules expressly permit this sixty-credit final year.
components: The mathematics course assumes pre-university Mathematics A knowledge; students with Mathematics A start its preparatory teaching earlier than students with Mathematics B.
Academic Basic Skills 1.2 requires completion of 1.1. Both are completed in the first year.

Second-year courses require at least 42 EC from Year 1. The experimental courses additionally require both Academic Basic Skills courses and Research Methods and Statistics; the review additionally requires both Academic Basic Skills courses. This pathway completes all 60 first-year credits first.
Philosophy of Science and Statistical Reasoning
The programming practical is completed before Experimental Psychology, as strongly recommended. Experimental Psychology and programming precede the EEG practical.
The second-year review is a literature study with an English report and presentation. It is a separate prerequisite for the later bachelor project.
Experimentation — Neurophysiology is the current name of the former Hodgkin & Huxley and Neuropharmacology practical; both names refer to the same requirement.

Thirty EC remain open for approved electives, a minor or exchange. No particular course or host is assumed. At most 12 EC of the elective space may be introductory first-year courses; outside courses require advance approval and must avoid excessive overlap. All first-year courses must be passed before third-year programme electives.

This example selects the permitted extended 30-EC scientific internship/project. Entry requires 120 EC one month before starting, including the full first year, Philosophy of Science and Statistical Reasoning, the second-year review and all five experimental practicals: programming, experimental psychology, EEG, molecular cell biology and neurophysiology. Completing both earlier years meets these conditions. The project includes supervised original research, an English scientific report and an English presentation; no host or research topic is assumed.

core: Psychobiology integrating biological and psychological explanations of brain, body and behaviour
Cellular, molecular and physiological neuroscience, including neurotransmitters and brain–body regulation
Cognition, perception, attention, consciousness, memory, emotion, motivation and decision-making
Experimental design, statistics, programming, data analysis, laboratory work and scientific reporting
Development, evolution and biological foundations of behaviour across the life course
Neurobiology of mental health, addiction, depression and atypical behaviour
adjacent: Cognitive neuroscience and computational analysis of perception, language and brain data
Molecular neuroscience, psychopharmacology and mechanisms of neurological or mental disorder
Evolutionary psychobiology and the evolution of behaviour and cognition
questions: How do biological processes in the brain and body generate cognition, emotion and behaviour?
How can experiments, brain measurement and data analysis reveal mechanisms of perception and behaviour?
How do molecular and neural mechanisms contribute to mental health, addiction and disease?

trace: develops academic writing, literature evaluation, research questions, reflection and collaborative civic practice
develops empirical design, measurement, sampling, statistics and a student data-collection project as foundations for experimental brain/behaviour inquiry
develops probability, Bayesian inference and sequential decisions under uncertainty as computational tools for modelling decisions; it does not itself establish biological decision mechanisms
develops logic, proof, discrete structures and formal modelling as mathematical foundations for computational analysis
develops algorithmic search and continuous/discrete optimisation, including implementation and experimental evaluation, as tools for computational modelling
develops algorithm design, complexity and data structures for implementing and evaluating computational analysis efficiently
develops data cleaning, transformation, visualisation and applied research in R for empirical biological and behavioural data
develops regression, classification, model evaluation and statistical prediction on real data, complementing experimental analysis
develops digital-image processing, segmentation, feature detection and recognition in Python as computational counterparts to studying visual information processing
develops artificial neural-network theory, model training and evaluation for image, text and time-series prediction; this computational contribution is distinguished from biological neural mechanisms
develops Python programming, structured problem solving and program testing for implementing experimental tasks and data workflows
develops calculus, differential equations and dynamic modelling as mathematical tools for quantitative biological and computational inquiry
develops probability distributions, inference, likelihood, Bayesian reasoning and simulation as a rigorous statistical complement to biomedical data analysis
examines selection, genetic variation, adaptation, phylogeny and evolutionary history, including a species project using Tinbergen’s four questions
examines mind, consciousness, identity, physicalism and neuropsychological cases through philosophical argument, complementing empirical neuroscience
examines free will, agency, determinism, addiction and scientific challenges to responsibility as conceptual complements to behavioural explanation
develops epidemiological design, bias, confounding and causality for studying disease patterns and evaluating biomedical evidence
examines human organ-system anatomy and functional spatial relationships through anatomical images and practical observation, supporting brain-body study
examines drug action, kinetics, metabolism, toxicity and pharmacogenomics, including nervous-system drugs and a psychoactive-drug research proposal
examines innate and adaptive immune mechanisms, host–microbe interactions and disease, including flow-cytometry analysis and research synthesis
connects normal organ function and regulation to endocrine, nervous-system and other disease mechanisms through clinical-case and pathophysiological analysis
examines comparative neuroanatomy, neurophysiology, animal behaviour, rhythms, sleep and mood/eating disorders, including laboratory introductions and animal-research ethics
examines neural mechanisms of sensory information processing and goal-directed action using cognitive-neuroscience and neuropsychological approaches
examines attention, memory, emotion, cognitive control and consciousness in relation to neural function and dysfunction, with an attentional-blink experiment and research proposal
examines neural and psychological mechanisms of language acquisition, comprehension and production, including impairments and experimental approaches
introduces cells, biomolecules, energy metabolism, DNA, heredity and gene expression as biological foundations for neuroscience
introduces neural signalling, brain anatomy, development, learning and behavioural/neuroscience research approaches as foundations for brain-behaviour study
examines cell regulation, gene expression, membranes, trafficking and signalling, including primary-literature analysis of a drug target
examines homeostasis, neuroendocrine signalling and integrated human organ-system regulation, supporting biological explanations of brain-body interaction
examines biomolecular structure, enzyme kinetics and metabolic pathways, linking biochemical defects to disease mechanisms
develops practical molecular, biochemical and microbiological techniques through protein purification, transformation, DNA analysis and reproducible laboratory reports
examines genetic and cellular disease mechanisms, inheritance, variation, epigenetics and molecular diagnosis, with a controlled research-grant proposal and ethics debate
examines social cognition, influence, group processes and behaviour through empirical research and a study proposal, providing a psychological context for cognitive neuroscience
develops experimental design and applied multivariable statistical models in health and behavioural research using data-analysis papers and a poster
examines mental disorder through biological, psychological, social and cultural explanations, with case analysis and a structured literature study
examines stress, illness, symptoms and health behaviour through biological, psychological and social interactions, supporting the brain-body and mental-health strand
develops systematic review and meta-analysis, effect sizes, heterogeneity, bias and research reporting in behavioural and medical inquiry
examines physical, cognitive, social and emotional development across the lifespan, including biological/environmental influences and a life-story study

alternatives.label: Brain, biology & behaviour
alternatives.concept: Study brain and behaviour through molecular and cellular biology, evolution, neurobiology, physiology and cognition. Combine laboratory work, empirical research and statistics with perception, development, mental health and the relationship between brain and body.
alternatives.labelReason: Study brain and behaviour through molecular and cellular biology, evolution, neurobiology, physiology and cognition. Combine laboratory work, empirical research and statistics with perception, development, mental health and the relationship between brain and body.
progression: Checked every offered term and earlier formal prerequisite against the current workbook. Brain and behaviour precedes cognitive courses; Neurobiology precedes Higher Order Functions. Statistical foundations precede meta-analysis, and data foundations precede machine learning and deep learning. Psycholinguistics is placed in its only planned term after Brain and Behavior, concurrently with Neurobiology, within UCR’s open progression rules.

alternatives.label: Cognitive neuroscience, perception & data
alternatives.concept: Study cognition, perception and language through neuroscience, experimental psychology and computational methods. Biological foundations and molecular cell biology support the brain-based focus; programming, statistical learning, image analysis and computational models provide complementary analytical methods.
alternatives.labelReason: Study cognition, perception and language through neuroscience, experimental psychology and computational methods. Biological foundations and molecular cell biology support the brain-based focus; programming, statistical learning, image analysis and computational models provide complementary analytical methods.
alternatives.distinctness: This option devotes sustained space to programming, mathematical and computational models, statistical learning and image analysis alongside cognition and neuroscience. The closest option instead gives greater weight to physiology, biochemistry, pharmacology, laboratory biology and clinical or health-related psychology.
progression: Checked every offered term and earlier formal prerequisite against the current workbook. Brain and behaviour precedes cognitive courses; Neurobiology precedes Higher Order Functions. Statistical foundations precede meta-analysis, and data foundations precede machine learning and deep learning. Psycholinguistics is placed in its only planned term after Brain and Behavior, concurrently with Neurobiology, within UCR’s open progression rules.

alternatives.label: Biological mechanisms, neuroscience & disease
alternatives.concept: Study biological mechanisms of brain and body function and disease through cell biology, biochemistry, genetics, physiology, neurobiology and pharmacology. Laboratory work and quantitative analysis support investigation of biological regulation, health and disorder.
alternatives.labelReason: Study biological mechanisms of brain and body function and disease through cell biology, biochemistry, genetics, physiology, neurobiology and pharmacology. Laboratory work and quantitative analysis support investigation of biological regulation, health and disorder.
alternatives.distinctness: This option concentrates on biological mechanisms, genetics, disease, pharmacology and laboratory science, with more biomedical and quantitative work. The closest option retains a broader psychological and developmental strand; the cognitive-data option concentrates on cognition, language and computational analysis.
progression: Checked every offered term and earlier formal prerequisite. Life-science and brain foundations precede dependent courses; cell biology precedes molecular pathology/genetics, Neurobiology precedes Higher Order Functions, and data science/machine learning precede deep learning.

selection.assessment: The closest programme combines substantial biological and neuroscience study with psychological and research content. Cognitive-neuroscience/data and molecular-neuroscience/health priorities are evidenced by official optional study packages and interests, not formal mandatory routes. Each implementation meets the pairwise thirty-EC floor and has a distinct substantive focus. Evolutionary psychobiology remains evidenced but is not attempted after the maximum of three.

blocks: Brain, biological mechanisms, behaviour and research
Both develop scholarly reading, academic writing, research questions, reflection and presentation. UvA specifically embeds these skills in psychobiological reporting.
Both develop research design, measurement, estimation, statistical testing and regression, with data analysis in R. UCR also includes a student research project.
Both develop programming in Python and implementation of executable tasks. UvA specifically programmes a visual-search experiment; UCR provides broader programming foundations.
Both develop scientific functions, calculus, complex numbers and differential-equation modelling as quantitative foundations.

Both examine evolutionary explanations of adaptation and behaviour, including natural selection, reproduction and Tinbergen’s questions. UvA concentrates more specifically on cognition and behavioural ecology.
Both examine consciousness, mind-body relations, reductionism and interpretations of neuroscience. UvA additionally provides a general cognitive-psychology introduction.
Both examine nervous-system anatomy and physiology in relation to behaviour. UvA also includes detailed membrane electrophysiology and peripheral organ-system anatomy and physiology.
Both examine sensory processing, visual perception and mechanisms linking perception to action. UvA also gives explicit attention to consciousness.
Both examine memory and higher cognitive functions through brain systems and experimental evidence. UvA extends much further into cellular mechanisms of learning and memory.
Both introduce neural organisation, biological and psychological processes, and relationships between brain function and behaviour.
Both examine molecular cell structure, bioenergetics, protein handling, membranes, trafficking and cell communication. UvA includes an integrated experimental practical.
Both develop hands-on molecular and biochemical laboratory skills, DNA/protein analysis and reproducible experimental reporting. UvA uses a specific glucocorticoid-receptor experiment.

Both examine inheritance, genetic variation, gene regulation and molecular mechanisms. UCR concentrates on human genetic disease; UvA also gives substantial coverage to population genetics and evolution.
Both develop multivariable statistical analysis, model choice and reasoned interpretation of behavioural evidence. UvA integrates this with philosophy of science and Bayesian reasoning.

Both develop substantial literature research, critical synthesis and scientific communication. UCR specialises in systematic review and quantitative meta-analysis; UvA’s review is a topic-based literature study.
Both examine cognitive and social development and biological/environmental influences. UvA additionally gives substantial coverage to embryonic development and molecular neurodevelopment.
Academic writing and research skills are represented elsewhere; no second course is counted as the separate continuation of the dedicated skills sequence.
Personal development is represented in the first-year skills placement; no additional course is counted as a separate study/career-orientation trajectory.

Selected courses develop experimental design and cognitive experiments, but their strongest primary placements are methods and cognitive functions; none is counted again as this dedicated student-run experimental-psychology practical.
Introductory neuroscience includes measurement perspectives, but no selected UCR course provides a dedicated EEG acquisition, analysis and reporting practical.
Ethics is considered in several selected courses, but none is a dedicated practical bioethics course across the scope of this component.
Selected laboratory and neurobiology courses provide complementary skills; none provides this dedicated combination of channel modelling and hands-on electrophysiological experiments.

Neurobiology, physiology and cognition address aspects of emotional and internal regulation elsewhere. No additional course is counted for this integrated emotion, reward, motivation and neurohormonal sequence.
Open elective space remains unspecified; no individual course, minor or exchange host is invented.
No compulsory 30-EC psychobiological research internship is scheduled at UCR. Optional independent research is displayed separately outside scheduled credits.

notes.text: UvA Psychobiology integrates biological and psychological study with dedicated EEG, molecular and neurophysiological practicals and a scientific internship. UCR can combine substantial biological, neuroscience, psychological and data study, but the partial course relationships do not reproduce this laboratory sequence or the selected 30-EC internship.

audience.programmeDescription: Psychobiology at UvA studies how biological processes in the brain and body relate to cognition, emotion and behaviour. Two compulsory years develop biology, neuroscience, psychology and research skills, followed by open electives and a scientific internship. This example selects the extended 30-EC project.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR can combine substantial biology, neuroscience, psychology and empirical methods. Its options prioritise a broad brain-and-behaviour response, cognition and computational analysis, or biological mechanisms and disease. UvA provides a more prescribed experimental sequence and a required psychobiological internship; the relationships shown are partial.
